links.title: Chapter 2: if-else and Flow Control - the lecture deck for this chapter
links.why: The slides this chapter is taught from: 83 slides, each with its talk track in the speaker notes. It sits in the chapter's own folder, one level above this page, and is renewed from the same research record and executed examples the page draws on.

links.title: 4. More Control Flow Tools
links.why: The tutorial's if, elif and else statements, where elif is short for else if and else is optional.

links.title: 8. Compound statements
links.why: The formal grammar of the if statement: one suite is chosen by testing conditions in order, with optional elif and else.

links.title: Built-in Types
links.why: Truth value testing, listing which objects count as false, plus the and, or and not table.

links.title: Built-in Functions
links.why: Documents bool(), which converts any argument to True or False by the standard truth testing procedure.

links.title: 6. Expressions
links.why: Chained comparisons such as x < y <= z, where y is evaluated only once.

links.title: operator — Standard operators as functions
links.why: Function forms of the comparison operators and of not, including operator.not_ and operator.truth.

links.title: 2. Lexical analysis
links.why: The indentation section, which explains how leading whitespace groups statements into blocks.

links.title: PEP 308 – Conditional Expressions
links.why: Specifies the X if C else Y form, where only one of the two branches is evaluated.

links.title: PEP 285 – Adding a bool type
links.why: Introduces bool as a subtype of int with the two values False and True, returned by comparisons.

links.title: PEP 8 – Style Guide for Python Code
links.why: Advises against comparing booleans to True or False with == and against one-line compound statements.

links.title: PEP 634 – Structural Pattern Matching: Specification
links.why: Specifies the match statement, which selects the first case whose pattern matches and whose guard is truthy.
